newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary shrs decline, BUX futures follow suit.
newsitem.headline: Hungary shrs decline, BUX futures follow suit.

text.p: Hungarian share prices drifted lower across the board on Friday adjusting themselves to more comfortable levels after sharp gains early this week.
The BUX index finished at 8,347.52 points, down 86.14 points or 1.02 percent.

"The market was cautiously retreating but after gains of three percent (a day) a one percent downward correction cannot be described as extreme," said Geza Raner of Bank Austria Invesment. "And there are still buyers for a lot of shares."
The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index, which more than doubled this year in forint terms, rose over seven percent in the first three days of the week.

On the futures market, BUX contracts closed lower for all maturities reflecting changes on the cash market, leaving yield contents roughly unchanged at around 20 percent for the two nearest maturities, traders said.
"As the (spot) index began to fall more than it did in early trading, futures more or less followed suit," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities.
September BUX ended at 8,502 points, down 98, while December gave up 100.5 points to close at 8,900.
Analysts said valuations of the Budapest bourse remain a decisive factor for further investments.
"Basically we've been positive on the Hungarian market all year and I'm not inclined to turn negative at this stage," said Mark Precious, analyst at SBC Warburg in London.
"We have increasing concerns about valuations, about how cheap the market is at this level, but I don't think it's due for a tumble."

Next week is expected to see batches of earnings reports. Most companies have scheduled submission of their first half figures for the last few days before the August 15 deadline, with only one-quarter having published them so far.

"If earnings do not start to come through to justify the valuations then I think Hungary would be struggling, however we are optimistic that the earnings numbers will come through as good," Precious said.
On Friday, oil company MOL finished at 4,980 forints, down 150; OTP Bank at 7,100 down 145; packaging firm Cofinec steady at 5,600; pharmaceuticals Richter up 20 to 21,120.
Confectionery retailer Bonbon finished 15 forints firmer at 470 forints despite reporting widening losses for the first half of 1997.
